title: DriveScape: Towards High-Resolution Controllable Multi-View Driving Video Generation
control_family: layout, box, map or BEV conditioning

output_modality.value: Multi-view driving video at 1024 x 576 resolution and up to 10Hz.

control_signal.value: BEV maps and 3D boxes projected to each camera view, BEV key-frames, neighbour-camera videos; also camera ID embeddings, canbus (velocity, direction) and a text scene prompt. Sparse conditions supported.

control_mechanism.value: Bi-Directional Modulated Transformer: condition-to-latent and latent-to-condition cross-attention with temporal self-attention, injected into the UNet; condition features come from convolutional encoders.

base_model.value: Latent diffusion with spatial-temporal UNet built on a pretrained Stable Video Diffusion model; spatial layers frozen, temporal layers and condition modules trained.

datasets.value: nuScenes: 700 scenes for training, 150 for validation; 8 object classes and 8 road classes.

metrics.value: FID, FVD, BEV segmentation (CVT; Road and Vehicle mIoU) and 3D detection (BEVFusion; NDS) on generated data.

controllability_evidence.value: Perception on generated validation data is lower than on real data: Road mIoU 64.43 (-9.25), Vehicle mIoU 28.86 (-5.98), Object NDS 36.5 (-4.71). FID 8.34, FVD 76.39. Qualitative map and layout edits shown.

closed_loop.value: No closed-loop rollout described; trained and evaluated on 8-frame video sequences.

stated_limitations.value: Future work: higher spatial-temporal resolution, a post-processing network to narrow the real-generated gap, strategies to cut memory overhead of multi-view inputs.

notes: Paper also claims mono-condition and multi-condition unified control; family chosen as layout/map/box conditioning. Closed-loop field reflects absence in packet only.
